fact: ITWeb reports that POPIA came into force on 1 July 2021 after a year-long grace period for organisations to comply.

ITWeb reports that the Information Regulator was established on 1 December 2016 to monitor and enforce compliance with POPIA and PAIA, and that its chairperson Pansy Tlakula and executives were speaking for it in September 2026.

The chairperson says the Regulator has moved from establishing the framework to exercising statutory enforcement powers, including receiving complaints, conducting assessments and issuing enforcement notices; no figures or named decisions are given (document published 2026-09-17, no event date).
The Information Regulator imposed its first fine, R5 million, on the Department of Justice and Constitutional Development for breaching POPIA, according to ITWeb quoting the Regulator.

The Regulator also fined the Department of Basic Education R5 million, and the Electoral Commission and Lancet Laboratories R100,000 each, both paid; the document gives no dates for these (published 2026-09-02).

ITWeb reports that the Regulator's enforcement powers came into force on 1 July 2021 after a year-long compliance grace period, and that POPIA provides fines up to R10 million and up to 10 years' imprisonment.
The Information Regulator's chairperson said it received over 3,800 complaints in the previous year, 10% of them on direct marketing (document published 2026-08-31, so the year read as 2025).
The Regulator has received over 8,000 security-compromise reports to date, 1,220 of them since April 2026, according to its chairperson at a 31 August 2026 briefing.

The Regulator issued the South African Bureau of Standards an enforcement notice the week before 31 August 2026 over its 2024 ransomware attack, finding POPIA conditions for lawful processing violated and giving it 90 days to revise policies, run impact assessments and implement security measures.
Two direct-marketing matters, involving OUTsurance and MTN, have been referred to the Regulator's enforcement committee under POPIA section 69 (reported 31 August 2026; no decision yet).

An Information Regulator commissioner said the Regulator receives complaints on processing without consent, direct marketing, breaches and deletion or correction requests, and can run compliance assessments on request or on its own initiative, but cannot test external systems before launch (webinar of 18 August 2026).
The commissioner said work is under way with the justice department to amend Popia to cover artificial intelligence and privacy by design; no bill or draft is described (18 August 2026).

After a November 2023 POPIA assessment the Information Regulator issued the basic education department a notice not to publish the 2024 matric results in newspapers; the department kept publishing exam numbers.
The Regulator lost three bids in the Pretoria high court to stop newspaper publication of matric results and has taken the case to the Supreme Court of Appeal (reported 17 August 2026).
The document says Popia was signed into law in 2013 and that the department stopped publishing learners' surnames in 2014 after Popia was established; it does not state a commencement date.

The Information Regulator published on 20 May 2026 an enforcement notice against Central Johannesburg TVET College, finding breaches of POPIA conditions for lawful processing and of the section 22 duty to notify security compromises, and ordering registration of information officers, notification of data subjects, an apology, a compliance framework and training within set periods.
The Information Regulator's Enforcement Committee applied POPIA sections 8, 15, 19 and 22 to a responsible party in a notice published on 20 May 2026.
The Information Regulator, through its Enforcement Committee, issued the POPIA enforcement notice of 20 May 2026 and runs an eServices Portal on which information officers are registered.

Regulations relating to the Processing of Data Subjects' Health Information by Certain Responsible Parties, 2026, made under section 112(2)(c) of POPIA, were published in Government Gazette 54268 on 6 March 2026 and commence on publication.
The regulations were made and signed on 27 February 2026 by Adv Pansy Tlakula as Chairperson of the Information Regulator.

Inside Privacy (Covington) describes POPIA as South Africa's data protection framework and states that its breach-notification and security-safeguard obligations currently bind responsible parties and operators.

The Information Regulator is stated to have announced on 7 April 2025 a requirement that breaches be reported through its eServices Portal, and receives breach notifications under POPIA, so it is an existing body acting.

The Information Regulator introduced an online eServices Portal as the official platform for POPIA security-compromise notifications; the document reports no sanction or decision, and says Form SCN1 for manual reporting was first released in 2023.
